title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 89
paragraphs: From this time onward the Argive and Aeginetan women, because of the quarrel with the Athenians, continued to wear pins larger than before, and still do so even to my day; and the origin of the Athenians' enmity toward the Aeginetans came about in the way described. So at this time, when the Thebans invoked them, the Aeginetans readily came to the aid of the Boeotians, calling to mind what had happened concerning the images. The Aeginetans then were laying waste, as I have said, the coastal regions of Attica; and when the Athenians resolved to make an expedition against the Aeginetans, an oracle came to them from Delphi bidding them wait for thirty years, reckoned from the time of the wrong done by the Aeginetans, and in the thirty-first year appoint a sacred enclosure for Aeacus and then begin the war against the Aeginetans, and they would succeed as they desired. But if they made an expedition against them immediately, they would in the meantime suffer very much evil and also inflict very much, but at last would subdue them. When the Athenians heard the report of this, they appointed a sacred enclosure for Aeacus—the one now established close to the marketplace—but they could not bear to hear that they must wait for thirty years, after they had suffered injuries from the Aeginetans.
